q1_issues.issue: "some" is recorded as a CardinalityPhrase, a form the instruction set reserves for the vague-count phrases it enumerates (a few / several / a handful / dozens / scores / hundreds / a lot of), while it routes "some" to the existential encoding instead.
The quantifier rides only the first coordinated group, leaving sk_group_2 with no quantifier record at all, so the two halves of one "Some X and Y" subject are encoded asymmetrically.
(Inheritance native_american native) exposes an origin/nationality modifier, which the compound-kind exposure list (gradable, positional/cardinal, or material adjectives only) does not license.
(Inheritance european_american_settler european_american) exposes the same kind of origin modifier and leaves a multi-word residue, whereas decomposition is specified to run to single-word lemmas.

q2_gaps: Bare "some" + plural noun as the subject of a verbal clause: the Existential section handles singular "some X" as one witness, the vague-count lexicon does not list "some", and the proportion route covers only generics and "of the" partitives, so no form is prescribed for a plural existential subject.

Capitalized multi-word KIND terms (ethnonyms/demonyms such as "Native Americans", "European-American settlers"): the multi-word-name rule (one opaque symbol, no genus, no modifier atoms) is written for proper nouns that carry a Name atom, and the instruction set never says whether it or the compound-kind decomposition rule governs a capitalized common-noun kind.

Scope of a determiner over a coordinated plural subject ("Some [A and B]" vs "[Some A] and [B]"): the coordination section says to replicate the predication per conjunct but gives no rule for distributing or scoping the determiner across the conjuncts.
notes: The inception frame (begin event, activity under Theme marked Ongoing), the distributive replication of the coordinated subject, and the omission of any LocatedIn on the created community all match the instruction set as written.
